svg.title: Dependency graph: what the refutation touches and what it cannot reach
svg.text: What the refutation touches -- and what it cannot reach
Red: refuted hypotheses and downstream external claims. Green: intact ground, including our entire foundation. Grey: false positives.
integer + real 3SUM, APSP / (min,+) product, Exact Triangle,
and dynamic-problem lower bounds built on them
SETH, Orthogonal Vectors, k-SUM/XOR for k at least 4,
our floor S = sqrt(pi/2A) + measured rho live here
all rest on the generic floor +
No floor, reference, or verdict moves.
1. Machine-found identities need machine-checkable certificates: the paper was discovered by Claude and verified in Lean 4/Mathlib.
We already do this for runs (replay receipts, sealed records); the gap is algebraic-identity claims. Proposal: identity claims ship a checker-replayable
certificate (Lean proof, or seeded independent re-evaluation) beside the claim. Next action: a follow-up PR writes the format into the study template.
2. Reductions are algorithms -- screen transfers on arrival via screen_workload (round 2), cited in future protocols, not this report.
3. Tiny-exponent polynomial gains do not move our verdicts by design: end-to-end S vs rho is exactly the filter such results must pass. Confirmatory, no change.
4. Watch the general regime (eps below 0.1204, paper Sec. 4), not just the concrete 1/18 line in the gate. Kept open from round 2.
Audit headline: no floor, reference, or verdict depends on a refuted hypothesis. A tree-wide hit showing otherwise would overturn this; the receipts above are the search that found none.
